extracted.intended_audience: federal legislators, administrative-law policymakers, social security tribunal administrators, and legal reform stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and procedural standards for reforming federal social security appeal processes and decision-making (creation of a new Federal Social Security Tribunal, procedural rules, decision-justification, handling of disability claims, and study of sanctioning powers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a new Federal Social Security Tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: A statute be enacted creating a new Federal Social Security Tribunal and determining its constitution, organization, jurisdictional authority and fundamental procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The new Tribunal would succeed to the jurisdictions exercised by the PAB, the Umpire and the Review Committees in matters of family allowances and Old Age Security pensions, and would in addition have certain powers presently exercised by the Tax Review Board." (specifies scope and successor bodies)

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct appeal within three months (except unemployment insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the sphere of unemployment insurance benefits, the Tribunal could be appealed to directly within 3 months of the rendering of an initial decision, without need on the part of the appellant to obtain leave to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies generally to social security appeals except explicitly for unemployment insurance benefits; establishes a firm direct-appeal time window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal as sole appeal authority (except unemployment insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except, again, in the sphere of unemployment insurance benefits, the Tribunal would serve as the one and only appeal authority for the contentious review of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The first level of contentious review in decisions concerning CPP benefits — the Review Committee — would be consequently abolished." (removes intermediate review bodies for CPP benefits)

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal hierarchical review preceding contentious review
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the present areas of the PAB's jurisdiction, the contentious review of cases would be invariably preceded by a process of internal, hierarchical review by the administrative authority that rendered the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The recourse provided by section 83 of the CPP in the sphere of benefits would be changed so as to make it subject to a six-month time limit within which a reconsideration committee, created by the Act and composed of senior officials and outside physicians, could be applied to for a ruling on the initial decision." (designates internal reconsideration mechanism and time limit)

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of all decisions (written reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: All administrative decisions should be justified in writing and specify the connection between the facts in the case and the rules of law that have been applied to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Our principal proposal with reference to the initial decision-making process calls for the justification of all decisions... We recommend that all decisions henceforth be justified in writing and that greater care be taken in describing the grounds on which they were taken." (responds to instances where notifications currently lack explanation or adequate legal-fact connection)

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical report forms to include Act requirements and disability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical report forms should be accompanied by an outline of the requirements of the Act as clarified and interpreted in PAB caselaw, and by a list of the criteria used in establishing disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation targeted at disability-pension decision-making to align medical evidence with statutory standards and tribunal interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give more weight to non-medical factors in disability pensions
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating disability pension claims more weight should be given to non-medical factors, especially the professional antecedents of the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to decision-makers to consider employment history and non-medical context alongside medical reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment hypotheses must account for claimant's personal situation and mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment hypotheses put forward to illustrate the claimant's residual work capacity should take more account of his personal situation, particularly the degree of his real geographical mobility in search of an employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how to construct realistic residual-capacity scenarios; emphasizes individualized assessment rather than generic assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations should contain a procedure section and be drafted simply
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations pertaining to each Act within the PAB's jurisdiction should contain a section devoted to procedure that governs the conduct of the decision-making and appeal processes and defines the rights and obligations of individuals participating in the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "They should be drafted in simple terms and a copy of them should be attached to application forms used by claimants to solicit a decision." (improves accessibility and transparency for administered persons)

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic study of sanction provisions to specify purpose and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A systematic study should be undertaken of provisions in federal law creating a power of sanction, with the particular object of specifying the purpose of administrative sanctions and the rules governing their imposition and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study should address: the relation between criminal and administrative sanctions; the imposition of administrative sanctions; methods of recovery used to exact penalties; waiver of sanctions by administrative authorities; and recourses open to the administered public against their imposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationalize appeal system via single supreme appeal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationalize the appeal system through the establishment of a single supreme appeal authority to reduce the disadvantages inherent in a complex sharing of administrative powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The institution of such a tribunal — open, accessible, independent and creative — can only advance the cause of administrative justice." (normative attributes expected of the new body)

rubrics_metrics.name: Address extraordinary slowness of appeal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The extraordinary slowness of the appeal procedure is identified as the most frequent and justified source of dissatisfaction with the present system and must be remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that both the Umpire and the PAB have proved unsatisfactory because of the slowness with which they dispense justice; reform proposals aim to speed resolution of appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure clear assignment of administrative responsibilities (Registrar duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative roles and responsibilities (for example the Registrar's duties) should be made clear and, where necessary, expressly provided for in procedural rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The Registrar has the same responsibility in other areas of the PAB's jurisdiction, even if the rules of procedure do not so provide expressly." (calls for express procedural provisions to avoid ambiguity)

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain systematic hearing records with specified data fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain systematic records of hearings including: file number, name and address of the individual concerned, place of the hearing, language used at the hearing, identity of the appellant, interventions, participation and representation of the parties, nature and tenor of the contested decision, subject of litigation, dates of successive phases of the procedure, the decision of the PAB, caselaw cited, observations made by the PAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation arises from sampling and is intended to support oversight, statistical analysis, and transparency of tribunal work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify relation between criminal and administrative sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the ends to be served by criminal versus administrative sanctions in administrative statute and examine whether certain conduct should be treated as criminal only when wilful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes discrepancies (e.g., section 123 of the Unemployment Insurance Act makes any violation an offence wilful or otherwise) and recommends theoretical and statutory analysis of sanctioning purposes, thresholds (wilfulness), and remedies.
